panels.assertion_heading: The published chain testifies against its own bounce
panels.narration: Act 1 begins with the chain. Its 4 papers produce 77 audit rows. The later bounce paper says the earlier spin-fluid foundation is “not self-consistent” and “violates the cosmological principle.” That is the paper's own verdict, not ours. 1 treatment uses repulsive stiff torsion and a smooth turning point; the other uses an attractive Dirac correction with a cusp-like velocity jump. They are incompatible mechanisms, not 1 bounce.

panels.assertion_heading: The 2 bounce treatments disagree by about 730
panels.narration: Re-derived separately, the 2 treatments disagree by about 730 on bounce density. Both calculate classically at or above the Planck scale, where classical theory is unestablished. This is no small parameter choice: 1 branch reaches a smooth halt before re-expanding, while the other has positive effective energy at its minimum and requires a prescribed jump. Any result that says “the bounce” without naming the branch hides the central fork.

panels.assertion_heading: An underived averaging choice swings torsion by exactly 6
panels.narration: The shared number has another fork. Both papers square the total fermion density, but neither derives that choice. Coherent versus independent species changes torsion density by exactly 6. The published value reproduces near the coherent edge; the better-motivated independent edge is 6 times smaller. We carry a bracket instead of selecting the endpoint, and every later result keeps that unresolved assumption attached.

panels.assertion_heading: The strict chain begins where the published spin bridge ends
panels.narration: Act 2 begins where print stops. Mass maps exactly into the interior's initial size, temperature, and angular extent, but parent spin has no published transfer function. Torsion couples to fermions' intrinsic spin, not a black hole's orbital angular momentum, so it cannot carry parent rotation alone. The published papers leave that vorticity-transport problem through the bounce unsolved. We bounded the missing bridge without inventing one.

panels.assertion_heading: Causality caps inherited spin near 1 part in 10 to the power 27
panels.narration: Demand the published homogeneous bounce of a rotating 10-solar-mass parent. If all parent angular momentum reached the bounce, rotation would overshoot the causal limit by a factor of 6.6 times 10 to the power 26. Self-consistency leaves at most about 1 part in 10 to the power 27, with the treatment branches spanning roughly 1 order of magnitude. Under Reading 2, rotating collapse never reaches this homogeneous solution at all; what happens instead remains underived.

panels.narration: Next, we tested whether the bounce could erase lopsidedness. Shear and torsion dilute at exactly the same rate, so their ratio is frozen. A bounce occurs only when shear is already subdominant; the bounce itself performs zero ironing-out. It cannot create an axis memory and it cannot erase it. Survival remains undetermined because the only proposed eraser is particle production, and that step is heuristic rather than derived.

panels.assertion_heading: Every generous confrontation still lands below every floor
panels.narration: Our torsion-density bracket sits 45 orders of magnitude below the published nucleosynthesis bound. That means consistency, not detectability. Then we stacked every generous choice for an axis signal. The treatment branches leave only about 10 to 100 parts per million of the perfect all-galaxy counting floor. That floor means counting all 2 trillion observable galaxies; it is a theoretical best, not an instrument. Conserving angular momentum directly makes the signal vastly smaller still.

panels.assertion_heading: The ceiling answers the axis question: nothing observable
panels.narration: We did not prove BHU cosmology false, and we did not test the wider family. We audited 1 published Popławski chain, kept its unresolved limits visible, and replaced its missing inheritance claim with the strongest ceiling its own homogeneous bounce permits. The frozen ratio supplies no hidden axis memory, and the all-galaxy floor leaves no observational escape. Asked through this published chain, the axis question answers: nothing observable. The strongest inheritance route now exists on the record as a ceiling, and the ceiling says the route stays closed.
